groups.title: columnscatter-radix-kernels
groups.mechanism: New (not in phj5) production column-wise radix scatter: rows are routed by a caller-computed 32-bit route word, each pass slicing a disjoint MSB-first bit range; histogram phase stores 2-byte partition ids that replace route re-reads; per-partition destinations are exact-size-allocated uninitialized (first-touched by scatter writes); column-major routing windows keep only fanout output streams live; at fanout >= 256 a software-write-combining path stages one 64-byte line per partition and flushes with non-temporal stores; computePassBits splits partition bits into balanced passes capped at MAX_FANOUT_PER_PASS. Also adds scatterWaves: a streaming windowed scatter+consume driver whose whole wave loop runs inside one pool dispatch with std::barrier phase separation and persistent per-worker scratch, plus dynamically-scheduled refine passes as skew defense.
groups.reason: The scatter kernel mechanisms are verified at AHJ_SHA in src/Columns/ColumnsScatter.h/.cpp, in a richer type-complete form: computePassBits (ColumnsScatter.cpp:1219, balanced MSB-first, MAX_FANOUT_PER_PASS=1024 per AHJ commit a630d83c74f), ScatterScratch with SWWC staging lines + drain and NT-store fence, SWWC_MIN_FANOUT=256, histogramPidChunk/reduceHistogramLanes lane interleaving, allocateUninitializedFixed (exact-size, no memset), plus String/Nullable/Tuple/Array/LowCardinality kernels the RBM version rejects. PartitionedHashJoinBuild.cpp consumes them in the same histogram -> allocate -> scatter phase structure (run_wave at lines 764-813; ColumnsScatter:: calls at 880-983). The scatterWaves barrier-wave probe driver specifically is NOT at AHJ — AHJ's probe is streaming per-block (PartitionedHashJoin::probeDispatch/probeImpl), a design difference; its evolution is the wave-machine group of a later shard.

groups.title: pipeline-lane-identity
groups.mechanism: Adds defaulted-forwarding IJoin virtual overloads addBlockToJoin(block, num_rows, check_limits, build_lane) and joinBlock(block, lane); FillingRightJoinSideTransform carries a build_lane and JoiningTransform a stream_index, assigned as simple counters in QueryPipelineBuilder::joinPipelinesRightLeft (per-outport lane, per-stream index). A join can then bind stable per-lane build/probe state with a plain array index instead of a lock-protected thread-id map or scratch pool; all nine existing IJoin implementers keep the forwarding default.
groups.reason: Absent at AHJ_SHA: git show AHJ_SHA:src/Interpreters/IJoin.h has no lane-carrying overloads, and AHJ's PartitionedHashJoin instead binds fill lanes via a mutex + std::unordered_map<std::thread::id, FillLane*> (getFillLane, PartitionedHashJoin.cpp:148-155, lane_by_thread at PartitionedHashJoin.h:323) and binds probe scratch via a mutexed pool (probe_scratch_mutex/probe_scratch_pool, PartitionedHashJoin.h:372-373). The pipeline-carried identity is a strictly cheaper and more deterministic way to get the same per-lane state.
groups.ahj_evidence: git grep 'lane' AHJ_SHA -- src/Interpreters/IJoin.h returns nothing; the only stream_index at AHJ's JoiningTransform.h belongs to NonJoinedBlocksTransform (a different feature). lane_by_thread map and probe scratch pool confirmed at AHJ as the current binding mechanism.
groups.expected_benefit: Removes one mutex acquisition + hash-map lookup per build block and one pooled acquire/release per probe scratch use, and makes the lane count deterministic (== pipeline streams) instead of growing per observed thread id. The source branch claims (commit message) it lets a join 'bind stable per-lane state without thread-local slot caches'; the wins are per-block, not per-row, so expect small absolute gains — mostly a simplification/determinism benefit.
groups.risk: Cross-cutting IJoin interface change touching all implementers, JoiningTransform, and QueryPipelineBuilder; documented caveat (source branch, risk R-a) that lanes are strictly below max_threads only for parallel FillRightFirst joins without right-side totals and are not guaranteed distinct across streams, so consumers must tolerate lane collisions — a silent-correctness trap if AHJ's per-lane state assumed distinctness.

groups.title: radix-hash-join-ijoin-core
groups.mechanism: The RadixHashJoin IJoin: zero-copy fill (right blocks accumulated per build lane, only per-leaf row counts taken), a lifecycle split where onBuildPhaseFinish does only the cheap barrier (concatenate lane stores, fold histograms — D-0003) and the heavy work (radix scatter of [ref|key] records, leaf layout/sizing, payload index) runs in runPostBuildPhase on a dedicated pool via new IJoin hooks hasPostBuildPhase/runPostBuildPhase; leaf hash tables are sized by per-leaf HLL distinct estimates (optionally reused across runs via HashTablesStatistics keyed on the plan, skipping the HLL when warm) and are built LAZILY at group granularity on first probe touch (ensureTouchedGroupsBuilt, first-toucher-wins with spinning contenders — D-0004).
groups.reason: PartitionedHashJoin at AHJ_SHA is the direct successor and carries the core mechanisms, verified: the IJoin post-build hooks exist (git show AHJ_SHA:src/Interpreters/IJoin.h lines 183-184 hasPostBuildPhase/runPostBuildPhase; PartitionedHashJoin.h:112-113 overrides them), the cheap-barrier/heavy-post-build split exists (PartitionedHashJoin.cpp:363-378 'the cheap barrier (R5)... heavy (scatter, hash-table allocation, leaf builds) runs in runPostBuildPhase'), zero-copy per-lane fill exists (PartitionedHashJoin.h:44 'blocks are accumulated per lane untouched'), and HLL-based leaf sizing exists (PartitionedHashJoinBuild.cpp:1319-1328 leaf_reserve from hll_estimate clamped by per-leaf row counts). Two sub-mechanisms did NOT carry over: (a) lazy first-touch group builds — AHJ builds all leaves eagerly in the post-build wave (run_wave leafBuildWorker, PartitionedHashJoinBuild.cpp:813); notably RBM itself later removed the lazy build (ensureTouchedGroupsBuilt is gone at RBM_SHA), so it is not a live port lead; (b) cross-run HashTablesStatistics reuse of the distinct-key estimate — absent at AHJ (git grep HashTablesStatistics in AHJ PartitionedHashJoin/ is empty) and still present at RBM_SHA; flagged in notes as a minor lead.
groups.ahj_evidence: Verified symbols at AHJ_SHA: IJoin.h:183-184; PartitionedHashJoin.h:112-113 (hasPostBuildPhase returns true), :44 (per-lane fill), :214 (per-lane DenseHyperLogLog); PartitionedHashJoin.cpp:363-378 (cheap barrier); PartitionedHashJoinBuild.cpp:813 (eager leaf-build wave) and :1319-1328 (HLL-derived leaf_reserve). groups.title: largest-first-partition-drain-order
groups.mechanism: Replaces size-oblivious index-order partition claiming in the probe wave with LPT scheduling: probeDrainOrder builds, once per wave after the scatter, the ids of partitions non-empty on both sides sorted by descending scattered row count (ties by ascending id), and the work-stealing fetch_add cursor indexes that array instead of 0..fanout. Starting the largest partition first keeps it off the wall-time tail under skew, and draining the biggest buffers first releases probe-window memory earliest. Same policy applied to the delayed-blocks final flush. Commit message claims 7-11% probe improvement on a constructed bimodal-imbalance shape, uniform shapes within noise.
groups.reason: The mechanism (largest-first dynamic claim of per-partition work under a work-stealing atomic cursor) is present at AHJ_SHA on the leaf-BUILD wave: git show AHJ_SHA:src/Interpreters/PartitionedHashJoin/PartitionedHashJoinBuild.cpp has `std::vector<UInt32> leaf_order; /// largest first` + `std::atomic<UInt32> leaf_claim` (lines ~388-389), sorts leaf_order by bucket_rows descending (line ~1346), and claims 'dynamically, largest first (G6)' via leaf_claim.fetch_add (lines ~1357-1364). The probe-side application specifically has no counterpart and cannot: AHJ's probe is unpartitioned ('probe blocks are never scattered or buffered', PartitionedHashJoin.h class comment), so there is no per-partition probe work unit to order — grep of PartitionedHashJoinProbe.cpp for drain/sort/largest finds nothing, correctly.

groups.title: wave-cooperative-drain-deadlock-fix
groups.mechanism: Replaces the per-result-owned probe wave (a std::unique_lock on wave_mutex moved into WaveJoinResult and held for its lifetime, with only that result's next draining the wave's bounded output queue) with a shared WaveCoordinator holding one refcounted ActiveWave: the lane that finds no active wave swaps out the shared probe window under the coordinator mutex, scatters it, and schedules dedicated pool workers that stream joined blocks into a ConcurrentBoundedQueue; every executor lane then pops from that queue cooperatively, so no lane waits on progress only another executor lane can make. Last-worker-out finishes the queue (mutex+condvar worker count); one lane wins torn_down.exchange and joins workers; abandoned waves are reaped by ~RadixHashJoin (clearAndFinish + joinWorkers). Also hardens parallelRun/startWave: on a mid-loop scheduleOrThrow failure it corrects the worker count for never-scheduled workers, finishes the queue, and joins before rethrowing (fixing a use-after-free), and keeps worker exceptions inside the job body so the shared pool is never poisoned. Claimed effect: unhangs multi-stream probes and 15-28% faster T96 payload-narrow shapes because the old design drained each wave through a single consumer.
groups.reason: PartitionedHashJoin's probe is unpartitioned and streaming by design: the class comment in PartitionedHashJoin.h at AHJ_SHA states 'probe blocks are never scattered or buffered; each row recomputes its route word and looks its key up in the routed leaf table'. There is no probe window, no wave, no producer pool, and no cross-lane output queue whose lifecycle could deadlock or need cooperative draining — the entire object this fix repairs does not exist. The one design-independent sub-mechanism (join already-scheduled jobs before rethrowing a scheduling failure) is already present at AHJ.

The scheduling-failure hardening equivalent exists at AHJ: PartitionedHashJoinBuild.cpp `run_wave` (approx. lines 735-756) and the locator-relocation stage (approx. lines 1262-1280) both wrap the scheduleOrThrow loop in try { ...; post_build_pool->wait(); } catch (...) { post_build_pool->wait(); throw; }.

groups.title: wave-bounded-consumer-cap-t16
groups.mechanism: Caps the executor lanes attached as consumers of one wave at max_consumers = max(2, threads/8) via a CAS attach loop on an atomic counter in ActiveWave (tryAttach/detach; detach in ~WaveJoinResult stays inert — plain atomic decrement, no waiting). A capped-out lane reports end-of-result and returns to pulling probe input while the shared window is below budget; once the window is staged to a full budget the lane attaches past the cap (restoring the pre-cap back-pressure, bounding window overshoot at one in-flight block per lane), and over-cap consumers dissolve at the next wave switch. Rationale: a pop costs a lane a work quantum, about 10x cheaper than producing the block, so ~3 consumers saturate the drain at T96 while sticky unbounded consumership at T16 captured every lane, ran the next wave with zero scanning lanes, and exposed a full ~116 ms window refill on the critical path (+11-12% bimodal regression).
groups.reason: This is a fix-of-the-fix for the cooperative wave drain introduced by 02b7ae9d93d: it tunes how many executor lanes are captured as queue consumers versus left scanning to refill the shared probe window. PartitionedHashJoin at AHJ_SHA has neither wave consumers nor a shared probe window to refill (probe blocks flow straight through the routed lookup in the calling lane), so the consumer/scanner balance problem cannot arise. The two commits are byte-identical twins of the same change committed independently on the two branches (verified: git diff b1fa64c7286 3fccb389f77 -- src/Interpreters/RadixHashJoin/RadixHashJoin.cpp is empty); b1fa64c7286 additionally carries the campaign's REPORT_T16.md/WORKLOG_T16.md verbatim.
groups.ahj_evidence: No consumer, attach/detach, window-budget, or wave symbols exist anywhere under src/Interpreters/PartitionedHashJoin at AHJ_SHA (scanned all 16 files); PartitionedHashJoin.h documents the unbuffered streaming probe that removes the mechanism's precondition.

groups.title: wave-worker-output-block-merging
groups.mechanism: Each wave pool worker accumulates its probe output into MutableColumns (insertRangeFrom after convertToFullColumnIfReplicated, since lazily-replicated columns cannot be appended to) and only pushes to the bounded queue once MERGE_TARGET_ROWS = 65409 rows or MERGE_TARGET_BYTES = 2 MiB is reached; disabled at threads == 1 where the producer is the critical path and the copy would be pure cost. Rationale: one popped block costs a consumer lane a full executor quantum (~235 us at T96 versus ~6.6 us inside next) regardless of block size, and the wave path emitted one tiny block per (partition, wave) — 393216 blocks of ~2.6k rows on the wide shape — so drain throughput was quantum-bound while producers sat 89% blocked; merging runs on producers that back-pressure keeps idle exactly when merging matters. Claimed -33.9% on D=268435456 r=4 bp=pp=7 T96 (11785 -> 7790 ms) with floors green. The merge commit 9c56f97e008 is the vehicle landing this code on the mainline: its src delta vs first parent is exactly this change, and vs second parent it only resolves REPORT_T16.md/WORKLOG_T16.md conflicts (no new mechanism).
groups.reason: The mechanism batches producer output before it crosses a thread boundary through a bounded queue to executor-lane consumers. In PartitionedHashJoin at AHJ_SHA no probe output ever crosses a thread boundary: joinBlock returns a JoinResult consumed in the same executor lane, output block granularity equals the input probe block (already pipeline-sized), and there is no queue and no consumer crew whose pop quantum could bound throughput. The pathology (orders-of-magnitude more tiny blocks than consumers) structurally cannot occur.

groups.title: cooperative-wave-probe-machine
groups.mechanism: Replaces the probe-side pool-producer/bounded-queue/sticky-lane design with one shared probe wave drained cooperatively by the executor's own probe lanes: admission is a single CAS on a packed atomic word [seal | in-flight | bytes] (budget check + reservation + in-flight count atomic together; the crossing admission seals); drain claims are single CASes on a packed control word [phase | generation | job-index] with each stage's last finisher running the barrier inline over the Preparing -> Scattering -> Refining -> Probing job graph; workers emit their own merged output (no shared queue/reorder buffer); first-exception-wins poisoning. a02a024c904 is a deadlock fix inside the machine (compare_exchange_strong overwrites its expected arg on failure, so tailOrWait slept on a mutated snapshot; fix: claim takes the word by value, the EOF-seal CAS uses a local copy). 05949c6f588 hoists ScatterScratch + pid buffer into WaveWorker so scatter jobs reuse per-worker scratch instead of allocating per job. c2f50791501 converts the sealing transition's single-owner exact sizing + per-partition column allocation into claimable per-partition Preparing jobs (source branch claims T96 -38..-40% wall on the wide target cell, and that the single-owner segment grew 312->1497 ms from T16 to T96).

groups.title: radix-hash-join-partitioned-build-foundation
groups.mechanism: Partition the build side by a per-row routing hash into leaf hash tables each sized to fit ~0.8x private L2 (PartitionPlan::choose), with a zero-copy fill that only accumulates blocks and per-thread histograms, then a deferred exactly-once multi-pass radix scatter of key+8-byte-ref (column-major, SWWC buffers + non-temporal stores at high fanout, balanced pass-bit split capped by max_partitions_per_pass) run cooperatively on the probe threads at the barrier (CoopPool leader+helpers), against jemalloc-backed exact-sized unzeroed Arena allocations. One 64-bit multiply-fold hash of the row-major packed fixed-width key drives both halves (high 32 bits = leaf route, low 32 bits = in-leaf bucket) so no per-row hash is stored; the probe recomputes it in 1024-row L1-resident tiles against per-leaf open-addressing tables (singleton-flag heads, lazily allocated chains) and gathers payload via per-(column,block) base pointers. Includes the enabling plumbing (radix_hash JoinAlgorithm value + max_partitions_per_pass setting + ProfileEvents) and the planner gate restricting to single-disjunct inner ALL equi-joins over fixed-width keys.
groups.reason: PartitionedHashJoin at AHJ_SHA is the direct successor embodying the same core, verified via git show AHJ_SHA: route-word hashing shared by build and probe in src/Interpreters/PartitionedHashJoin/JoinRouteHashing.h (computeJoinRouteWords / computeJoinRoutesForFill / computeJoinLeafIds); L2-sized leaf plan (decidePartitionPlan in PartitionedHashJoinBuild.cpp; class comment 'smallest power of two whose worst-case per-leaf bucket array ... fits the private L2 cache'); deferred cooperative histogram+scatter (histogramWorker/allocateWorker/scatterWorker/refinePassWave over src/Columns/ColumnsScatter.h kernels with SWWC_MIN_FANOUT=256, MAX_FANOUT_PER_PASS=1024 and computePassBits using the same balanced remainder-first split as PartitionPlan::choose); exact-sized unzeroed one-slab leaf allocation (src/Interpreters/PartitionedHashJoin/FixedRegionAllocator.h, replacing the jemalloc Arena); largest-first leaf claiming (leaf_order/leaf_claim in PartitionedHashJoinBuild.cpp); planner gate PartitionedHashJoin::isSupported; plumbing JoinAlgorithm::PARTITIONED_HASH (src/Core/Joins.h:131), 'partitioned_hash' in SettingsEnums.cpp:62, PartitionedHashJoin* ProfileEvents (ProfileEvents.cpp:436-445). groups.title: amac-probe-ring
groups.mechanism: Replaces the streaming per-row find with AMAC: a ring of 16 in-flight probe-row state machines (Stage Scan/Chain), each performing exactly one memory-dependent step per visit and software-prefetching the address of its next visit, so 16 independent cell/chain accesses stay outstanding and DRAM latency overlaps across the data-dependent open-addressing walk and duplicate-chain walk. Each slot resolves its leaf at pull, so no shared probe scratch; emitted match set is order-permuted only. Commit claims ~12x probe-stage demand LLC miss reduction (30.9M -> 2.5M) and parity with parallel_hash (1407 ms vs 1442 ms) on a 200M x 400M join.

groups.title: probe-output-plan-scratch-pool-and-block-sorted-payload-gather
groups.mechanism: Three probe-emit optimizations: (1) OutputPlan precomputes the output schema once (left columns, payload columns by index, required right keys copied from left); (2) a mutex-pooled per-probe-thread ProbeScratch (ScratchHandle RAII) whose buffers only grow, so the steady-state probe does no per-block heap allocation; (3) sortMatchesByBlock counting-sorts matched (left_row, ref) pairs by build block into contiguous BlockRuns so each build block's payload is gathered with one bulk IColumn::index call per run instead of random per-match block hops.

The headline mechanism (3) is absent: ahj's emit path (HashJoin/AddedColumns.cpp fillFromRowRefs, HashJoinResult.cpp) resolves row refs in probe order with per-row block resolution, no counting sort into per-build-block runs. groups.title: tagged-word-row-ref-cells-and-per-worker-build-arenas
groups.mechanism: Replaces the bespoke next_chain row chaining with a single tagged 8-byte cell word (DB::BuildRefList): a unique key stores the encoded build ref inline (MSB flag), the first duplicate allocates an arena Batch node and the word becomes a pointer, so the probe emits singleton matches with zero extra loads and walks a compact node list otherwise. Duplicate-node arenas move from per-leaf to per-build-worker (vector of Arena indexed by a dense worker id from the parallel-for, single writer each), decoupling arena count from leaf count.
groups.reason: Verified via git show AHJ_SHA:src/Interpreters/RowRefs.h — `RowRef::encode`/`RowRef::INLINE_FLAG` (bit 63 marks an inline singleton ref word) and `RowRefList` as a tagged 8-byte word (48-bit pointer to an arena `Batch` node plus a saturating 15-bit count in bits 62..48) are the direct, further-evolved descendants of BuildRefList; PartitionedJoinMaps.h static_asserts the leaf cells use exactly these mapped types. Per-worker arenas verified: `std::deque<Arena> build_arenas` (PartitionedHashJoin.h:357), one arena emplaced per worker in `postBuildPartitioned` (PartitionedHashJoinBuild.cpp:719-721), consumed single-writer as `Arena & pool` by `AmacBuildInsertPolicy`.

groups.title: eager-threadpool-postbuild-and-8-byte-packed-leaf-descriptor
groups.mechanism: Two mechanisms. (1) The heavy post-build (scatter, leaf-table build, index setup) runs eagerly on a dedicated ThreadPool (scheduleOrThrow + wait, dynamic work-stealing on an atomic cursor, fixed dense worker ids) right after the build barrier instead of being deferred cooperatively onto the first probe threads, so joinBlock never builds. (2) The per-leaf descriptor LeafHT packs log2(num_buckets) into the low 6 bits of the 64-byte-aligned cells pointer, shrinking the descriptor from 16 to 8 bytes; num_buckets/mask are recovered once per probe row, never in the AMAC inner step.
groups.reason: Mechanism 1 is already present at AHJ_SHA: `post_build_pool` (std::unique_ptr<ThreadPool>, PartitionedHashJoin.h:362) runs staged waves in `postBuildPartitioned` (PartitionedHashJoinBuild.cpp:723-749), driven eagerly by `FillingRightJoinSideTransform::work` -> `runPostBuildPhase` (JoiningTransform.cpp:360) before any probe. Mechanism 2 is ABSENT: the flat per-leaf descriptor `LeafMapDesc` at AHJ is 16 bytes `{const void * buf; size_t mask}` (PartitionedHashJoin.h:34-38), not a packed 8-byte word — so only the descriptor packing is the port candidate.
groups.ahj_evidence: git show AHJ_SHA:src/Interpreters/PartitionedHashJoin/PartitionedHashJoin.h shows LeafMapDesc {buf, mask} = 16 bytes; the probe's flat loop comment (PartitionedHashJoinProbeImpl.h ~line 603) states the contiguous 16-byte-per-leaf descriptor array is the address-generation critical path, and probe slots copy desc.buf/desc.mask at admit. Eager pool post-build fully present.
groups.expected_benefit: Halving the leaf-descriptor array (16 -> 8 bytes per leaf) doubles descriptor L1 density on the per-row desc gather that ahj's own comments place on the probe's address-generation critical path. Source branch claims (as claims): probe time unchanged (~10.1 s) with the packed descriptor, i.e. no regression from recovering mask via (1 << bits) - 1 once per row.
groups.risk: Must guarantee 64-byte (or at least 2^6) alignment for every leaf cell buffer, including FixedRegionAllocator heap fallbacks, or reserve fewer low bits; ahj leaf maps are growable, so the descriptor must be republished on cursorGrow; the empty-leaf zero-word sentinel needs mapping onto ahj's always-materialized leaf maps. Moderate-low.

groups.title: amac-probe-slot-slimming-and-ring-deepening
groups.mechanism: Incremental slimming of the AMAC probe ring slot to raise memory-level parallelism without stack spills: two-value Stage enum collapsed to a bool then folded into an existing slot field (non-null cells pointer = active), power-of-two &-mask ring wrap, and finally a 16-byte slot {cells ptr, UInt32 pos, UInt16 row, UInt8 bits} where the key pointer is recomputed from row and mask from bits, with a PosT=UInt32/UInt64 template dispatch on max_bucket_bits, letting the ring deepen from 16 to 32 in-flight rows.
groups.reason: Verified via git show AHJ_SHA:src/Interpreters/PartitionedHashJoin/AmacRing.h: `AmacRingSlot<false>` is static_asserted to 16 bytes, activeness is encoded in an existing field (`row == inactive_row` sentinel, no separate flag — the same fold-activeness-into-slot-data idea), `amac_ring_size = 32`, and the slot-minimalism rationale is documented ('a fat slot spills the ring state to the stack and kills the memory-level parallelism'). The steady phase even supersedes the &-mask wrap with a plain full-array sweep (no wrap arithmetic and no per-visit active check). The routed probe slot extends only with admit-resolved address material (buf/mask/leaf, sizeof(Slot)==32 or 48), a documented measured tradeoff of the same idea.

groups.title: hash-keys-once-inside-the-amac-pipeline
groups.mechanism: Probe: the per-row 64-bit key hash moves out of an upfront pack/hash pass into the ring's pull_next, so the multiply-fold latency overlaps the outstanding cell misses of the other in-flight slots; the hashes scratch array and hashRun pass are deleted. Build: fillLeaf hashes each key exactly once by ping-ponging two home-bucket buffers (cur/nxt) so the bucket survives until insert, and leafInsertAt starts the linear probe at the precomputed bucket instead of re-hashing.
groups.reason: Verified at AHJ_SHA: the probe has no upfront hash pass — the AMAC probe policy's `start` computes `const size_t hash = map0.hash(key)` at admit (PartitionedHashJoinProbeImpl.h ~line 189) and the flat non-AMAC loop hashes inline in its look-ahead prefetch; the build's `AmacBuildInsertPolicy::start` hashes once at admit and seeds `slot.pos = map.cursorPlace(hash)` (PartitionedHashJoinBuild.cpp ~line 144). Where recomputation is expensive the hash is carried in the slot (`cell_stores_hash` in AmacRing.h — string cells carry saved_hash); cheap keys deliberately recompute to keep the 16-byte slot, a documented refinement of the same never-hash-in-a-separate-pass idea. Note: commit 85b56431df5852849b2294245f805ed950cf07ed's full hash is 85b56431df5852849b2294245f805ed... (short id 85b56431df5).

groups.title: shared-adaptive-amac-ring-for-probe-and-build
groups.mechanism: Unifies the probe's AMAC pipeline and the build insert's group/look-ahead prefetch onto one generic amacRing driver: a power-of-two round-robin of in-flight rows where each visit performs exactly one memory-dependent step and prefetches the single address the next visit dereferences, including every data-dependent collision step. A Policy supplies the slot type and per-visit step (ProbePolicy read-only; BuildPolicy fused read-then-mutate in one indivisible visit so two in-flight same-key rows can never both claim an empty cell); loop-invariant leaf state is hoisted out of the build slot (8 bytes {pos,row}).
groups.reason: Verified via git show AHJ_SHA:src/Interpreters/PartitionedHashJoin/AmacRing.h: the `amacRun` driver with Policy-supplied `Slot`/`start`/`step`, the fused read->act invariant documented verbatim ('the cell read and the resulting mutation MUST be one indivisible visit'), one-prefetch-per-visit discipline over collision steps, and both policies exist — the probe policy in PartitionedHashJoinProbeImpl.h and `AmacBuildInsertPolicy` in PartitionedHashJoinBuild.cpp. AHJ extends the shared driver beyond phj5 with growth cancellation (`amacDrainAndGrow`, needed because its leaf maps are growable) and a frame-copy SSA opt-in (`copy_into_frame`/`writeBackTo`).

groups.title: hll-distinct-estimate-leaf-table-sizing
groups.mechanism: Sizes each leaf's hash table by a HyperLogLog distinct-key estimate instead of raw row count, clamped so it can only shrink a table (duplicate-heavy builds get smaller, cache-hotter tables); per-worker dense-only sketches are fed during the scatter's last pass from the low 32 hash bits (independent of the leaf-selecting high bits) and register-max merged. The follow-up fix keeps one guaranteed-empty cell per fixed-size leaf (refuse the claim that would fill the last cell, flag, and rebuild that leaf once with safe row-count sizing) so an HLL under-estimate can never make the non-growable open-addressing walk loop forever.
groups.reason: Verified at AHJ_SHA: DenseHyperLogLog.h is the same dense-only sketch (registers, rank, register-max merge, bias + linear-counting corrected harmonic mean, plus an fmix32 finalizer refinement); per-lane sketches are fed during fill and merged at the barrier (`merged.merge(lane.hll)` in PartitionedHashJoin.cpp `onBuildPhaseFinish`); leaf reserve = clamp(hll_estimate * reserve_safety / partitions, 1, leaf rows) with the explicit invariant comment 'The sketch estimate can only shrink a leaf below its row count, never inflate it' (PartitionedHashJoinBuild.cpp:1318-1328), and the degenerate single-leaf plan exact-reserves from the sketch (line 631). The ed390b infinite-loop hazard does not exist at AHJ because the leaf maps are growable standard maps: an under-reserve triggers grower overflow -> `cursorGrow`/`amacDrainAndGrow` (AmacRing.h) with a counted, never-silent FixedRegionAllocator heap fallback — the under-estimate safety is provided by growth instead of the refuse-last-cell rebuild.
groups.ahj_evidence: git show AHJ_SHA:src/Interpreters/PartitionedHashJoin/DenseHyperLogLog.h; PartitionedHashJoinBuild.cpp lines 627-646 and 1318-1329; AmacRing.h cursorGrow/amacDrainAndGrow; FixedRegionAllocator.h heap_fallbacks. Difference: phj5 kept per-leaf per-worker sketches; AHJ keeps per-lane global sketches and rescales uniformly per leaf, clamped by the exact per-leaf histogram — equivalent given route-hash uniformity.

groups.title: warm-run-cached-distinct-estimate-skips-hll
groups.mechanism: On a warm run, a dedicated RadixHashJoinEntry{distinct_keys} in the cross-run HashTablesStatistics cache (kept separate from ConcurrentHashJoin's HashJoinEntry so the two algorithms never clobber each other's entry for the same query key) supplies the join's distinct-key count, so the per-leaf HLL estimation is skipped entirely: per-leaf estimates are reconstructed by rescaling the cached global count by the exact per-leaf row histogram, clamped to [1, rows]. The cold run publishes the fresh estimate. Gated by collect_hash_table_stats_during_joins; a stale value only mis-sizes (detected and repaired), never breaks correctness.
groups.reason: Absent at AHJ_SHA: git grep finds no HashTablesStatistics/StatsCollectingParams usage anywhere under src/Interpreters/PartitionedHashJoin (PlannerJoins.cpp builds StatsCollectingParams only for the other join algorithms), and HashTablesStatistics.h has only AggregationEntry and HashJoinEntry — no partitioned-join entry. AHJ computes the HLL from scratch on every run, fed inside the fill route-word loop.
groups.ahj_evidence: git grep 'HashTablesStatistics|StatsCollectingParams' AHJ_SHA -- src/Interpreters/PartitionedHashJoin returns nothing; git show AHJ_SHA:src/Interpreters/HashTablesStatistics.h lists only AggregationEntry/HashJoinEntry.
groups.expected_benefit: Skipping the per-row sketch add in the fill loop on warm runs, plus a plan-stable distinct estimate. The source branch claims ~11% faster warm-run build on a 200M-distinct uniform build (cited as a claim, under phj5's architecture where the HLL ran inside the scatter); AHJ's benefit would be smaller since its sketch feed is already fused into the route-word fill loop, but it is nonzero per-row work on every build row.
groups.risk: Low. Estimate errors only affect sizing (clamped per leaf, and AHJ's maps grow on under-reserve — though growth defeats the slab exact-prediction, so a bad cached value could increase heap_fallbacks/regrowth). Needs a dedicated cache entry type keyed apart from HashJoinEntry, and plumbing StatsCollectingParams into the PartitionedHashJoin constructor. Also interacts with AHJ's partition-plan choice, which consumes hll_estimate at the barrier — the cached value must arrive before plan selection.

groups.title: byte-balanced-leaf-cell-allocation
groups.mechanism: Replaces per-leaf arena allocations in buildLeafTables with three passes: (A) serial per-leaf sizing + exclusive byte prefix sum; (B) a few chunk-sized allocations whose boundaries are byte-balanced across workers (lower_bound on the byte prefix), each chunk carved into 64-byte-aligned per-leaf cell bases; (C) parallel fill that memsets each leaf's cells immediately before filling it, preserving cache-hot first-touch and dynamic skew balancing. Cuts allocator churn from O(num_leaves) allocations to O(num_workers).
groups.reason: Verified via git show AHJ_SHA:src/Interpreters/PartitionedHashJoin/FixedRegionAllocator.h - class FixedRegionAllocator carves every leaf map's buffer out of ONE contiguous unzeroed slab ('ONE allocation per build'), and its alloc zeroes exactly the leaf's buffer 'right before the map fills it' so pages are first-touched cache-hot. git show AHJ_SHA:src/Interpreters/PartitionedHashJoin/PartitionedHashJoinBuild.cpp lines ~1319-1368 show exact per-leaf predicted sizes (predictedBufferBytes through the grower math), a leaf_offset prefix over one ht_slab allocation, and workers claiming leaves dynamically largest-first (leaf_order/leaf_claim). This is the same mechanism in a stronger form (one slab instead of a few chunks).

groups.title: grouped-leaves-metadata-compression
groups.mechanism: Quantizes per-leaf hash-table sizes into at most 2^MAX_GROUP_BITS=256 consecutive homogeneous leaf groups: within a group every leaf is snapped to the LARGEST member's bucket count and all leaves share one contiguous allocation, so a leaf's cell base is computed arithmetically as group_base + local * roundUpToLine(nb * stride) from a <=256-entry (<=2-4 KB, one page, L1-resident) descriptor table instead of gathering from an up-to-8 MB per-leaf descriptor vector. The probe's only metadata load becomes an L1 hit; group id = route >> (32 - group_bits).
groups.expected_benefit: AHJ's probe admit gathers a 16-byte LeafMapDesc from a flat per-leaf array (leaf_descs[leaf], PartitionedHashJoinProbeImpl.h:190) - 16 B/leaf, e.g. 64 KB at 4K leaves, beyond L1, and a data-dependent load on the critical admit path. The session's project memory claims this leaf_map_descs gather is the probe's stall center (recorded as causal, 2026-07-19) - cited as a claim. The source branch claims the grouped table is L1-resident (<=256 entries) versus an up-to-8 MB per-leaf vector; porting would convert the probe's metadata gather into an L1 hit plus arithmetic.
groups.risk: Real design friction: AHJ leaf maps are standard HashJoin maps that can GROW past their reserve (FixedRegionAllocator heap fallback moves the buffer off the slab), which breaks arithmetic base derivation and needs an escape path; per-leaf reserves are clamped by per-leaf row counts (PartitionedHashJoinBuild.cpp:1328) so group-max quantization wastes slab memory; masks vary per leaf today and must become group-uniform. Feasible (the slab is already carved in leaf-id order) but not a drop-in.

groups.title: amac-probe-pipeline-unification
groups.mechanism: Unifies the probe into a single AMAC software-prefetch ring for every key width, bucket-index width, and duplicate-ness: a 32-slot power-of-two ring where admit resolves the row's leaf descriptor + home bucket and issues the home-cell prefetch, each visit does exactly one dependent cell read (steady/drain split: no per-visit active check or modulo while rows remain), a singleton match emits the encoded ref word directly from the just-read cell (no second load), duplicates go through a cold-outlined BuildRefList walk, and matches are written through growable raw cursors kept in registers. Internally this group is an introduce-then-revert arc: 1fb3eb0d32e added a tiled, multitarget-vectorized generateSeeds pre-pass hoisting hash/route/address into an L1 seed stream (measured claim: probe 38.98 -> 29.78 ns/row at 1B rows); a1607631ded dropped the redundant PROBE_BATCH_ROWS batching and moved the seed arrays into reusable caller-owned scratch; 48880389173 then removed the seed pre-pass entirely - after the hash became CRC32 (874fce9ca06) 'that pre-pass is no longer worth the seed-buffer traffic' - inlining hash/route/address back into admit (probeHomeCell).
groups.reason: The end-state mechanism (the shape that survived on the source branch) is verified at AHJ_SHA: src/Interpreters/PartitionedHashJoin/AmacRing.h - amacRun implements the steady/drain split ('no per-visit active check, no modulo'), 32-slot power-of-two ring, refill/pull skeleton, and amacDrainAndGrow; AmacRingSlot is kept minimal with per-slot address material allowed at admit. src/Interpreters/PartitionedHashJoin/PartitionedHashJoinProbeImpl.h - RoutedAmacFindPolicy resolves the leaf's buf+mask once at admit from the flat LeafMapDesc array and carries them in the slot; the matched mapped value is copied BY VALUE (found_word) in the same visit that reads the cell so the cell is never touched again - the same 'singleton emits directly, no second load' idea. AHJ also hoists the route/leaf-id derivation into a per-block vectorized pre-pass (computeJoinLeafIds in JoinRouteHashing.h) - the surviving half of the hoisting idea - while the bucketing hash stays inline at admit, exactly matching 48880389173's final shape. The transient generateSeeds tile pre-pass is absent at AHJ, but it was reverted on the source branch itself, so nothing beneficial is missing.

groups.title: crc32c-packed-key-hash
groups.mechanism: Replaces the 64-bit multiply-fold ('mum'/wyhash-style, 2+ rounds) packed-key hash with a 32-bit CRC32C HashT: widths matching an integer type (1,2,4,8,16,32 B) hash via HashCRC32<T> on the loaded value, composite widths via updateWeakHash32 over the byte span; route and bucket both slice the single 32-bit word under a total_bits + log2(buckets) <= 32 budget. Much cheaper per row on the hot bucketing path (hardware CRC32 instruction vs chained 128-bit multiplies), which in turn made the probe's seed pre-pass unprofitable (see 48880389173).

observations.finding: RBM's central probe mechanism: a cooperative budget-bounded wave machine (ProbeWave). mechanisms.name: Generic AMAC ring driver (amacRun)
mechanisms.details: Power-of-two ring of `amac_ring_size = 32` slots (static_assert has_single_bit); engagement floor `amac_min_rows = 256`. Policy contract: `Slot`, `may_grow`, `start(slot,row)->bool` (seed hash + home-cell prefetch; false = handled synchronously, slot stays free), `step(slot)->AmacStepResult{Advance,Done,DoneNeedsGrow}` (ONE fused read->act per visit). Steady/drain split: while every refill succeeded the steady phase sweeps the ring with a plain array for-loop (no per-visit active check, no modulo); first failed refill or row exhaustion drops to the drain loop with the active check. Justification comment cites Kocberber et al., PVLDB 2015 (8-10 in-flight rows saturate L1-D miss handling; >32 slots risks TLB thrash).

mechanisms.name: ResumableHashMap cursor API + growth cancellation
mechanisms.details: `ResumableHashMap<Base>` DERIVES from the standard join HashMapTable (cells/hash/grower unchanged, probe machinery sees a standard map) and exposes the decomposed emplace/find: `cursorPlace(hash)`, `cursorNext(pos)`, `cursorCell`, `cursorCells` (buffer base for caching), `cursorCellIsEmpty`, `cursorKeyEquals`, `cursorClaim` (= emplaceNonZeroImpl up to the mapped write; returns grower overflow), `cursorGrow` (= resize). Growth is a ring cancellation point: `amacDrainAndGrow` (ALWAYS_INLINE, called inside steady loop to avoid capture-induced reloads) collects in-flight rows, deactivates, grows, re-seeds in slot order so same-key rows still act in row order; chassert that re-seeding never fails (sync-handled rows never entered the ring). Load-bearing invariant documented: cell read and mutation must be one indivisible visit or two in-flight same-key rows could both claim an empty cell.

mechanisms.name: Measured slot minimalism (AmacRingSlot)
mechanisms.details: `AmacRingSlot<false>` = {size_t pos; UInt32 row} with inactive sentinel row=UINT32_MAX; static_assert sizeof == 16. `AmacRingSlot<true>` adds `size_t hash`; static_assert sizeof == 24. `cell_stores_hash<Cell>` concept (requires cell.saved_hash): string-key cells carry the hash in the slot (recompute expensive + keyEquals prefilter); cheap-key getters recompute from the reloaded key keeping the slot at 16 bytes. Everything recomputable from the row index is recomputed per visit; per-section invariants live in the policy.

mechanisms.name: Frame-copy policy opt-in + compile-time AMAC gate
mechanisms.details: `copy_into_frame` opt-in: `amacRun` runs on a frame-local copy of the policy so its fields become SSA values that stores through result arrays cannot alias (behind a reference they would be conservatively reloaded per visit); mutable aggregates return via `writeBackTo` invoked after the drain (skipped on exception). Gate `amac_join_supported<KeyGetter,Map>` = `AmacResumableMap<Map>` (cursor API present) AND NOT LowCardinality getter (its own per-dictionary-index dedup cache would fight the ring) AND NOT HashMethodHashed (recomputes 128-bit serialized-key hash per fetch); FixedHashMap key8/key16 excluded by having no cursor API (no collision chain to pipeline).

mechanisms.name: Dense HyperLogLog sketch for leaf-table sizing
mechanisms.details: `precision = 13`, `register_count = 8192` UInt8 registers = 8 KiB per fill lane, ~1.15% standard error covered by `reserve_safety = 1.2`. Fed the 32-bit route word of every non-null build key; per-lane sketches merged once at the build barrier (register-wise max). Input is self-finalized with murmur fmix32 (0x85ebca6b, 0xc2b2ae35) - a bijection - because the multiply-shift route fold's middle bits are not avalanche-quality. Estimate = bias-corrected harmonic mean, alpha = 0.7213/(1+1.079/m), precomputed ldexp table of 33 inverse powers, linear-counting correction when raw <= 2.5m and zeros > 0.

mechanisms.name: One-allocation slab with per-leaf region carving
mechanisms.details: Hash-table allocator carving each leaf map's buffer from ONE contiguous slab (requirement: one allocation per build). Thread-local `pending_region` arming: worker arms {begin, bytes, carve/fallback atomic counters}, constructs the map, and the map's single buffer alloc adopts the region if size <= region.bytes, `memset(region_begin, 0, size)` zeroing exactly the requested bytes (slab allocated unzeroed; pages first-touched cache-hot right before the fill). Size mismatch or later growth (distinct-estimate shortfall) fails over to heap - counted via `heap_fallbacks` atomic, never silent; `realloc` out of region copies to zero-filling heap alloc; `free` of a region buffer is a no-op (released with the slab). Unarmed maps (key8/key16) behave like plain HashTableAllocator.

mechanisms.name: Route-word computation (build/probe shared contract)
mechanisms.details: One 32-bit route word per row over the join keys, deliberately independent of the CRC32C the leaf maps bucket by (imported ColumnsScatter route-word family: `routeWord`, `foldBytes`, `mixStep`, `finalizeRoute`). Hot path: single numeric fixed-contiguous key dispatches by width 1/2/4/8 to `routeSingleNumericColumn<T>` (exact benchmark-proven `routeWord` per value); restricted to numeric so cross-representation pairs (FixedString vs LowCardinality) take the byte fold. Multi-column: `RouteColumnKind{Fixed,String,LowCardinality,Generic}` classified once per column, column-outer accumulation into a `PaddedPODArray<UInt64>` accumulator (per-column dispatch hoisted out of the row loop), then `finalizeRoute` per row. Generic uses vectorized `computeHashInto` (value-based, representation-independent). LowCardinality routes by value bytes = identical words to a plain column of the same values.

mechanisms.name: Fused route loops (fill + probe)
mechanisms.details: Both public entry points instantiate ONE template `computeJoinRouteWordsImpl` with a compile-time-known `sink(row, word)` inlined into the loops (no 32-bit word transient). Fill (`computeJoinRoutesForFill`, commit 49ea5e243c0): stores `word >> 16` as UInt16 route for ALL rows (scatter reads skipped rows' routes too) and feeds the full word to the lane HLL only where `skip` does not filter. Probe (`computeJoinLeafIds`, commit 55fb661acf4): stores leaf id `word >> (32-bits)` directly per row (chassert 0 < bits <= 16). Build's stored route slice `route >> (16-bits)` and probe's leaf id agree on the shared top bits for every plan.

mechanisms.name: LeafMapDesc flat lookup descriptors
mechanisms.details: 16-byte `LeafMapDesc{const void * buf; size_t mask}` per leaf in one contiguous array (`leaf_map_descs`), extracted once after the builds by `collectLeafMapPointers`: per-row cell address = one L1 load + `hash & mask` instead of chasing `leaf_map_ptrs[leaf]` then the map header (three dependent loads on the address-generation critical path; comment explicitly mirrors parallel_hash's contiguous bucket-header array). key8/key16 keep the zero entry (their probe never takes the descriptor path). Also `leaf_map_ptrs` (type-erased map pointers) built once so the probe does not rebuild an 8B x partitions pointer table per joinBlock.

mechanisms.name: Per-thread fill lanes + FillBlock accumulation
mechanisms.details: Fill phase: `std::deque<FillLane>` + `lane_by_thread` map guarded by `fill_mutex` only for lane acquisition; each lane holds `std::vector<FillBlock>` + its own DenseHyperLogLog - append and sketch update contention-free. FillBlock: payload block in row-store form (zero-copy `prepareRightBlock`), prepared key columns (nested, merged null map extracted, live LowCardinality kept only for dictionary-aware map types), `join_mask` right-side ON condition, merged `skip_bytes` (null OR mask, materialized only when the mask filters), saved `PaddedPODArray<UInt16> routes`. `accumulated_rows/bytes` relaxed atomics feed the size-limits check.

mechanisms.name: Narrow 4-byte locator encoding
mechanisms.details: `narrow_locators`: when block count <= 2^16 and every (block_no, rows) fits 16+16 bits, the scattered locator column uses packed UInt32 `(block_no << 16) | row_no` decoded to the 8-byte `RowRef` word only at insert - halves the largest scatter transient. Otherwise 8-byte encoded `RowRef` words (`encode()` = block_no<<32|row_no with INLINE_FLAG bit 63). Decided once at the build barrier.

mechanisms.name: Shared per-offset used-flag space (flag_base)
mechanisms.details: One flag space spans all leaves for RIGHT/FULL/SEMI/ANTI/ANY used flags: `flag_base[L]` = prefix sums of per-leaf `getBufferSizeInCells() + 1` (the +1 covers the zero-value cell, matching standard sizing); size partitions+1. Probe shifts every FindResult offset by its leaf's base before `processMatch`, so `JoinUsedFlags` and non-joined iteration keep single-map semantics; `used_flags->reinit` runs once after leaf builds (`computeFlagBaseAndReinitUsedFlags`); `flag_base` cleared for shapes without right-side flags (visible to tests).

mechanisms.name: Parallel zero-insert fill phase
mechanisms.details: `supportParallelJoin() = !delegate_mode`: right-side streams call `addBlockToJoin` concurrently; no hash-table insertion during fill - only key prep, fused route+HLL, and a lane append. ASOF routes/sketches by the equi-key prefix only (trailing inequality column excluded). Fill-phase limit check against accumulated rows/bytes. `delegate_mode` (multiple disjuncts, per-row-flags regime) runs the standard HashJoin whole - single fill stream, partition plan 1.

mechanisms.name: Cheap build barrier + L2 partition plan
mechanisms.details: `onBuildPhaseFinish` (last fill thread): concatenate lanes, assign row-store block numbers (`storeBlocksInRowStore`, also saving nullmap/ON-mask holders for RIGHT/FULL non-joined), merge HLL sketches, decide plan; heavy work deferred to `runPostBuildPhase` (`hasPostBuildPhase() = true`). `decidePartitionPlan`: smallest `bits <= 16` such that `predictedBufferBytes(maps_variant, type, ceil(hll_estimate*1.2 / 2^bits))` fits `0.8 * L2` (grower-exact rounding; L2 floor 1 MiB); once bits>0, parallelism floor `bit_width(bit_ceil(num_threads)-1)` so leaf builds parallelize; ASOF and FixedHashMap types (key8/key16) pinned to the single-leaf degenerate plan; small builds degenerate too (bits stays 0).

mechanisms.name: Multi-pass scatter plan (pass_bits)
mechanisms.details: `pass_bits = ColumnsScatter::computePassBits(partitions, max_fanout_per_pass)` splits bits into MSB-first passes when the L2 rule wants fanout above the per-pass ceiling. At AHJ_SHA `ColumnsScatter::MAX_FANOUT_PER_PASS = 1024` and `computePassBits` is a BALANCED split (per_pass = ceil(total_bits/num_passes)) - commit a630d83c74f restored balanced, reverting the greedy MSB-first split of f11bc53a918. 16-bit plan-loop bound is exactly what UInt16 routes and UInt16 probe leaf ids cover - no route widening at any reachable plan. Test hook `setMaxFanoutPerPassForTests` lets small builds exercise refine passes.

mechanisms.name: Stage-wave post-build pipeline with dedicated pool
mechanisms.details: `postBuildPartitioned`: dedicated ThreadPool of `workers = min(num_threads, num_blocks)` threads; stages run as waves with `pool->wait()` barriers: histogram -> allocate -> scatter -> refine passes (multi-pass only) -> planAndAllocateHashTables (caller thread) -> leaf builds. Each job accrues thread time into `PartitionedHashJoinBuildMicroseconds` (unit-compatible with parallel_hash's summed thread time) plus per-stage wall/thread ms in a TRACE log; sub-phase events `BuildHistogramMicroseconds` (hist+prefix-sum), `BuildScatterMicroseconds` (scatter+refine), `BuildLeafMicroseconds` (plan+inserts). Block stripes: `blockStripe(w) = [w*n/W, (w+1)*n/W)`.

mechanisms.name: Histogram stage with interleaved lanes + drop bucket
mechanisms.details: `deriveBucketIds`: bucket = `routes[i] >> (16-bits)` from the SAVED routes (key columns untouched); skipped rows (null keys, ON-mask) go to drop bucket index `partitions` (fanout = 2^route_bits + 1), scattered like any bucket and freed before the leaf builds. `histogramWorker` uses `ColumnsScatter::histogramPidChunk` with a 4-lane interleaved histogram (`hist_lanes_mem` = 4*fanout) when fanout <= `HIST_INTERLEAVE_MAX_FANOUT = 2048`, reduced by `reduceHistogramLanes`.

mechanisms.name: Fused prefix-sum + exact uninitialized chunk allocation
mechanisms.details: `allocateWorker`: buckets striped across workers; per bucket, running prefix sum over per-worker histograms fills `starts[p*workers + w]` (bucket p holds worker w's rows at [starts, starts+hist)), then ONE exact allocation per (bucket, scattered column): `resize_exact` for locators/routes, `ColumnsScatter::allocateUninitializedFixed` for fixed-width key columns (exact reserve, no power-of-two growth) - pages first-touched by the scatter writes themselves, not by the allocation.

mechanisms.name: Cooperative SWWC scatter with batched memory cycling
mechanisms.details: `scatterWorker`: per-(column,bucket) cursors seeded at `starts[p*workers+worker]`; SWWC (software write-combining, 64-byte staging lines in `ScatterScratch`) when fanout >= `SWWC_MIN_FANOUT = 256` and `widthSupportsSwwc(width)`; kernels are `ColumnsScatter::scatterPidChunk(width, pids, data, rows, swwc, scratch)`. Fused batching: whole-block batches sized `scatterBatchRowsTarget(fanout) = max(256Ki rows, fanout*64 lines*8)`; bucket ids derived once per block and shared by all scattered columns; a batch's input chunks (keys, routes, null maps, masks) are released as soon as their last column is scattered. Locators synthesized in L2-resident pieces of `locator_piece_rows = 32768`. Multi-pass plans also scatter the 16-bit route words alongside (same layout). Generic mode (String/LowCardinality/exotic): type-complete Layer-1 `ColumnsScatter::scatter` into self-contained per-(column,worker,bucket) pieces; null-bucket piece dropped immediately.

mechanisms.name: Multi-pass refine waves (lifts the fanout cap)
mechanisms.details: `refinePassWave` (commit 1e351cee5c9): splits each current bucket (group) into 2^refine_bits sub-buckets by the next MSB-first route slice `(route >> (16-bits_done-refine_bits)) & (sub_fanout-1)`, group-major output `leaf = (group << refine_bits) | sub` - final leaf index equals `route >> (16-bits)`, identical to a single-pass plan and to the probe's derivation. Groups claimed dynamically via `std::atomic<size_t> next_group.fetch_add` (skew tolerance); per-group inputs (locators, routes, key chunks) freed as soon as consumed - memory cycles instead of doubling the scattered side. Route words re-scattered only when another pass follows; generic mode consolidates per-worker pieces into ONE self-contained piece per (column, leaf).

mechanisms.name: Slab plan: exact grower prediction, 64B-aligned regions, largest-first order
mechanisms.details: `planAndAllocateHashTables`: per-leaf reserve = clamp(ceil(hll*1.2/partitions), 1, bucket_rows[leaf]) (sketch can only shrink, never inflate); `leaf_bytes` from `PartitionedJoinMaps::predictedBufferBytes` = the map's own `grower.set(reserve); grower.bufSize()*sizeof(cell)` so predicted == actual (asserted via `stats.predictions_exact`); leaf offsets rounded up to `LINE_BYTES = 64`; ONE `Allocator<false,false>` slab alloc (unzeroed, not pre-faulted), `stats.slab_allocations` counts real allocation calls; `leaf_order` sorted by bucket_rows descending for largest-first claiming. Single-leaf path (`postBuildSingleLeaf`) allocates the same way for one region and inserts straight from stored blocks with `RowRef(block_no, i)` refs.

mechanisms.name: Dynamic largest-first leaf claiming + per-worker arenas
mechanisms.details: `leafBuildWorker`: leaves claimed via `ctx.leaf_claim.fetch_add(1)` indexing `leaf_order` (largest first) - skew can never serialize the build on worker-partition affinity. Per leaf: arm `FixedRegionAllocator::Region{ht_slab + leaf_offset, leaf_bytes}`, create the map (buffer carved + zeroed in-region), insert sections (cooperative fixed chunks; or per-worker generic pieces in worker order matching the cooperative locator layout; or one refined piece), then release the leaf's scatter chunks immediately. One `Arena` per worker (`build_arenas`) holds string keys and RowRefList duplicate nodes for the life of the maps.

mechanisms.name: AMAC build-insert policy (fused claim step)
mechanisms.details: `AmacBuildInsertPolicy<KeyGetter,Map>`: `start` computes the map hash (latency overlaps other slots' misses) + `__builtin_prefetch(cells+pos, 1, 3)` (write intent, high locality); zero-sentinel keys handled synchronously via standard `emplace` (never occupy a slot). `step` is one fused read->act: empty cell -> `cursorClaim` + mapped write in the SAME visit (a later same-key/colliding row can never also see it empty); key match -> `applyBuildRowToMapped` (RowRefList inline-first/arena-append via `insert`; RowRef first-or-last with any_take_last_row); else advance + prefetch next cell. `cells` buffer base cached in a policy field (one add off a register per visit), refreshed by `grow`. `copy_into_frame = is_copy_constructible_v<KeyGetter>` (commit 472b9a23beb) with `writeBackTo` returning {all_unique, growths}; KeysFixed getter (non-copyable prepared-keys buffer) stays by-reference. Growth counted in `amac_ring_growths` stat/ProfileEvent.

mechanisms.name: Build engagement heuristics + sequential fallback with look-ahead prefetch
mechanisms.details: `decideAmacEngagement` (once, right after the slab is sized): `amac_enabled && leaf_join->enableSoftwarePrefetch() && ht_slab_bytes > getMinBytesForPrefetchInJoin()` - aggregate slab size is the scale (build streams scattered chunks through cache alongside its leaf). Per-section row floor `rows >= amac_min_rows (256)`. Below/ineligible: sequential emplace loop with `makeJoinPrefetcher` look-ahead (gated on `join_prefetch_supported` and map size > threshold). ASOF always sequential single-leaf (sorted per-key vectors want original block/row order; insert order not fused-one-cell). `insertSectionImpl` mirrors `insertFromBlockImplTypeCase` + Inserter semantics exactly; `applyBuildRowToMapped` is shared by the sequential and AMAC paths so both stay identical.

mechanisms.name: Kind/strictness dispatch + RightAny promotion + per-kind TU split
mechanisms.details: `probeDispatch` mirrors the MapGetter table: INNER{All/RightAny/Any/Asof}, LEFT{All/RightAny/Any/Semi/Anti/Asof}, RIGHT{All/RightAny/Any/Semi/Anti - all MapsAll}, FULL{All/RightAny - MapsAll}; `prefer_use_maps_all` (build barrier promoted ALL->RightAny on an all-unique build) probes the ALL-built RowRefList maps with RightAny semantics, skipping replication like hash/parallel_hash. Template bodies in ProbeImpl.h, explicitly instantiated in 4 per-kind .cpp files (Inner/Left/Right/Full) to keep each TU small. Unreachable combos throw LOGICAL_ERROR.

mechanisms.name: Unpartitioned routed probe over standard emit machinery
mechanisms.details: Probe blocks are never scattered, buffered or materialized (G2): `routedJoinRightColumns` is the single-map `joinRightColumns` loop with each row's map = leaf `word >> (32-bits)`. Leaf ids computed once over the WHOLE source block (`computeJoinLeafIds` into pooled `ProbeScratch.leaf_ids`; continuation chunks share it), only when bits > 0 - the single-leaf plan pays zero extra allocation (scratch acquired lazily from the mutex-pooled `probe_scratch_pool`, returned via SCOPE_EXIT). Everything downstream is standard HashJoin machinery: `AddedColumns`, `processMatch`, skip bytes merging null map + ON mask with a fast-path that compiles the check out, `offsets_to_replicate`, lazy `HashJoinResult` emit over the shared row store.

mechanisms.name: RoutedAmacFindPolicy - two-phase probe, phase A
mechanisms.details: Find-only AMAC ring filling per-row result arrays out of order; `may_grow = false`, `copy_into_frame = true`. Slot extends AmacRingSlot with {UInt16 leaf; const Cell * buf; size_t mask} resolved ONCE at admit from `leaf_map_descs` (commit f412c470ab1) - static_assert sizeof(Slot) == 32 (48 with stored hash); a steady visit dereferences nothing but the cell and the probe key. Records the matched cell's mapped value BY VALUE into `found_word` (commit a42de56262a): RowRef encodes / RowRefList IS an 8-byte word, never 0 for a built cell (INLINE_FLAG bit 63 or non-null node pointer), so 0 = miss and phase B never touches the cell again; ASOF-style non-word mapped stores the pointer bits. `found_offset` = `slot.pos + 1 + flag_base[leaf]` computed without touching the map, recorded only for flagged shapes. Prefetch read intent, low locality (0,1). Selector variant (range vs indexes) is a template parameter (was a per-visit load). static_asserts pin `is_power_of_two_linear_grower` + `HashTableNoState` cells; skipped/zero-key rows recorded synchronously in `start`.

mechanisms.name: Degenerate phase B: dispatch-free word_loop
mechanisms.details: Gate `degenerate_phase_b = AddedColumnsType::isLazy() && amac_mapped_fits_word && !need_flags && !is_asof_join && !is_any_join` (commit a00bfcb642a): consumes `found_word` directly instead of rebuilding a FindResult and dispatching `processMatch` per row (whose outlined `appendFromBlock` call forced loop-carried state to spill). Raw cursor writes into pre-sized arrays with no per-append capacity check: `filter_data[i]`, `*matched_cur++`, `*ref_cur++` (row_refs resized to rows upfront, trimmed after); ALL appends the list word advancing the replication offset by `refWordRows(word)`; RightAny/Semi appends `firstRefWord`; anti-join handled flagless. `rows_local` copy avoids the loop bound reloading through the closure (filter byte stores may alias). Non-degenerate shapes run the same in-order full loop with the lookup replaced by the precomputed result (`mappedFromWord` rebuilds the mapped value on the stack; cell never dereferenced again); 3-way parity suite pins equivalence.

mechanisms.name: flat_loop: flat-descriptor sequential probe with invariant snapshotting
mechanisms.details: For cheap-key open-addressing maps below the AMAC threshold (commit 2322bdca1f5), gated by concept `FlatLookupMap` (power-of-two linear grower + stateless cells). Two structural fixes per the probe disassembly: (1) per-row cell address from the contiguous `LeafMapDesc` array - inline `HashMapTable::find`: `pos = hash & desc.mask`, walk `(pos+1) & mask`, offset = pos+1 (identical semantics); (2) every loop invariant (selector base, leaf ids, skip data, flag base, descriptors, by-value key-getter copy) snapshotted into locals because closure fields sit behind a pointer conservatively reloaded after every opaque call (~10 per-row loads observed). Selector variant is a template parameter. Look-ahead prefetcher hashes into `desc.buf + (hash & mask)`. Zero-sentinel keys resolve through the map object (rare).

mechanisms.name: AMAC probe engagement + measured wins
mechanisms.details: `use_amac = amac_enabled && added_columns.enable_prefetch && ht_slab_bytes > getMinBytesForPrefetchInJoin() && rows >= 256 && rows < UINT32_MAX`; above the threshold the ring is the single engaged probe path for every AMAC-capable shape (commit a00bfcb642a; earlier gate 48c605b6ef4 engaged it only where look-ahead cannot run). Documented measurements: string-key maps (look-ahead prefetch cannot run - getKeyHolder per look-ahead too expensive) ~20% faster end-to-end (T16 and T1); cheap-key getters ~11% probe thread time at T16, parity-to-win at T1 after slot-carried address chain + degenerate emit removed per-visit metadata/two-phase costs. Look-ahead prefetch of the plain/flat loop is mutually exclusive with AMAC, same L2-based threshold. Test hook `setAmacEnabledForTests` pins the sequential loops for cross-checks.

mechanisms.name: Direct typed gather emit with prebuilt raw-data tables
mechanisms.details: `added_columns.lazy_output.use_direct_typed_gather = true` for non-Any, non-ASOF lazy shapes (commit c2e702f8d61) - fixed-width right columns emitted via a direct typed gather instead of the generic pair-expansion path; partitioned-only by construction (hash/parallel_hash never set the flag). Backing tables prebuilt in the emit table (commit fd53e4e604e): `StoredColumnsIndex::EmitColumn.data_by_block` (raw `getRawData` base per block) + `sample_column` (one typeid_cast validates the whole table), handed to LazyOutput as `DirectGatherColumn{data_by_block, sample_column}` - resolving per emit call would put blocks x columns cold typeid_cast chains on every output chunk (the dominant probe cost of a large build with narrow probe blocks).

mechanisms.name: NotJoinedPartitioned: resumable leaf-order non-joined stream
mechanisms.details: RIGHT/FULL non-joined filler over the leaf maps in leaf order; per-cell used check at `flag_base[leaf] + map.offsetInternal(cell)` - exactly where the probe marked it. Resumable across `fillColumns` calls: `current_leaf` + `std::any position` iterator into the current leaf's map, `max_block_size` rows per call; `collectMapped` mirrors CollectorNonJoined (every ref word of an unused RowRefList via encoded-word iteration, single row of a RowRef). Never-inserted rows (null keys, ON-mask misses) come from the nullmap holders saved at the barrier (`fillNullsFromBlocks`). Delegate mode falls back to `NotJoinedHash` via the leaf join.

mechanisms.name: Allocator-rebind leaf maps with cell bit-identity asserts
mechanisms.details: `WithRegionAllocator<HashMapTable<K,Cell,Hash,Grower,Alloc>>::Type = ResumableHashMap<HashMapTable<..., FixedRegionAllocator>>` (FixedHashMap rebinds allocator only, no cursor API): leaf map types are DERIVED from `HashJoin::MapsTemplate` members with only the allocator rebound, so master-side cell/hash/grower changes propagate automatically and incompatible restructurings break the build. 13 map types (`APPLY_FOR_PARTITIONED_JOIN_VARIANTS`): key8, key16, key32, key64, key_string, key_fixed_string, keys32/64/128/256, hashed, low_cardinality_key_string/fixed_string - single-level subset of HashJoin::Type (two-level and range conversions gated off). static_asserts pin cell_type identity to HashJoin::MapsOne/MapsAll/MapsAsof per type; `PartitionedJoinMaps` is a std::variant<PartitionedMapsOne/All/Asof> static_asserted index-compatible with HashJoin::MapsVariant. `predictedBufferBytes` = grower.set(reserve) -> bufSize()*sizeof(cell), or full key-domain size for FixedHashMap.
