mechanisms.name: Route hashing family (partition routing decorrelated from bucket hashing)
mechanisms.details: routeWord(UInt64): on aarch64 with __ARM_FEATURE_CRC32 it is __crc32d(-1U, key) (ISO-polynomial CRC32, NOT the CRC32C the leaf tables bucket with — deliberate decorrelation so partition assignment does not skew in-leaf bucket placement); elsewhere golden-ratio multiply-shift (key * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15) >> 32. Wide/composite keys: foldBytes = 8-bytes-at-a-time mixStep((h^x)*0x9E3779B97F4A7C15) with a switch-dispatched constant-size tail copy (cases 1..7, zero-padded chunk, bit-identical to a runtime-size copy but no per-row libc memcpy); finalizeRoute(h) = h>>32; routeWordBytes(p,w) = finalizeRoute(foldBytes(0,p,w)). All passes of a multi-pass plan slice disjoint bit ranges of this ONE 32-bit route word, consumed MSB-first via (word >> shift) & mask.

mechanisms.name: Multi-pass split policy: computePassBits — BALANCED split (not greedy MSB-first) with MAX_FANOUT_PER_PASS = 1024
mechanisms.details: Constants at AHJ_SHA: LINE_BYTES=64, SWWC_MIN_FANOUT=256, HIST_INTERLEAVE_MAX_FANOUT=2048, SCATTER_BATCH_MIN_ROWS=256<<10, SCATTER_BATCH_LINES_PER_PARTITION=64, MAX_FANOUT_PER_PASS=1024 (SWWC staging ~76 B/partition/worker must fit L2; also why UInt16 pids suffice per pass); scatterBatchRowsTarget(fanout)=max(SCATTER_BATCH_MIN_ROWS, fanout*64*8). computePassBits (ColumnsScatter.cpp): chassert(has_single_bit(fanout)); total_bits=countr_zero(fanout); pass_bits=log2(bit_floor(max(2,cap))); num_passes=ceil(total/pass_bits); per_pass=ceil(total/num_passes); emits min(per_pass, remaining) until exhausted. Header doc: "balanced across passes (e.g. 15 bits under a 10-bit per-pass cap split 8 + 7, not 10 + 5)". IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the reported state: commit f11bc53a918 introduced a greedy MSB-first split, but the later commit a630d83c74f RESTORED the balanced split while raising MAX_FANOUT_PER_PASS to 1024; so at AHJ_SHA the sizing is balanced — only bit CONSUMPTION order is MSB-first (route word sliced from the top).

mechanisms.name: ScatterScratch: SWWC per-worker scatter state with persistent cursors (the chunk-peel/reuse API)
mechanisms.details: Fields: fanout, use_swwc, PaddedPODArray<char> staging_mem (fanout*64 + 64 bytes, manually aligned up to a 64-byte boundary), char* staging, PaddedPODArray<char*> cursors (byte-granular), PaddedPODArray<UInt32> fill. Invariant: staged bytes of partition p live at staging + p*64 + [m, fill) with m = cursor&63; seed(p,cursor) initializes fill[p] with the cursor misalignment; the first line flush of a misaligned stream emits the partial head (LINE_BYTES - m bytes) with REGULAR stores, after which the cursor is line-aligned and full lines go out as one __builtin_nontemporal_store of a char __attribute__((vector_size(64))) NtLine. drain() flushes each partition's residual [m, fill) bytes with memcpy and issues atomic_thread_fence(seq_cst) to publish weakly-ordered NT stores. Reuse protocol: init once, seed once per column, scatter all chunks (cursors persist across chunk calls — call overhead per chunk never per row), drain once; setUseSwwc toggles the path between columns without reallocating. widthSupportsSwwc: only w ∈ {1,2,4,8,16} (widths dividing the 64-byte line under the 16-byte column-data alignment guarantee); SWWC engaged only when num_shards >= SWWC_MIN_FANOUT=256.

mechanisms.name: Fixed-width scatter kernel variants (compile-time width dispatch + SWWC/direct pair)
mechanisms.details: Route sources as template policies: RouteFromKey<width,Pid> (computes (routeWordFixed<width>(key)>>shift)&mask and OPTIONALLY writes pids[i] when pids != nullptr — the in-kernel route/pid-emit fusion), RouteFromKeyGeneric<Pid> (runtime width), RouteFromPids<Pid>. Bodies: scatterDirect<width> (plain per-partition byte cursors, __builtin_memcpy_inline of the constant width), scatterSwwc<width> (staging-line accumulate, flush at fill==64; staging/cursors/fill pointers hoisted to locals because the char*/vector NT store defeats TBAA hoisting), scatterOne<width> picks SWWC vs direct at runtime. Width switch in scatterKeyChunkImpl: cases 4/8/16 via scatterOne, case 32 (UInt256/Decimal256) direct-only (not SWWC-eligible), default -> scatterDirectGeneric with copyRowExact. scatterPidChunkImpl switch: 1/2/4/8/16 via scatterOne, 32 direct, default generic. routeWordFixed<8> uses __builtin_memcpy_inline + routeWord (the CRC path); other widths fully unroll foldBytes.

mechanisms.name: copyRowExact: runtime-width exact-byte row copy from constant-size copies (32-byte chunk stride)
mechanisms.details: For w>=16: loop of __builtin_memcpy_inline(dst+i, src+i, 32) chunks with an inline-asm "memory" barrier per chunk (chosen so the backend pairs loads/stores — ldp/stp on AArch64 — while the barrier defeats clang loop-idiom re-materialization of a per-row libc memcpy), then one 16-byte step if it fits, then one OVERLAPPED trailing 16-byte copy at dst+w-16. Sub-16 widths: overlapping constant-size pairs (8/8, 4/4, 2/2, single byte). Never touches a byte outside [dst, dst+w) — preserves the exact-sized-destination contract. Sibling copyRowAllowOverflow15 (String kernel): 16-byte strides with the same barrier, MAY write up to 15 bytes past the end (memcpySmallAllowReadWriteOverflow15 contract; __msan_unpoison_overflow_15), documented as recovering ~8% of String-kernel bandwidth on aarch64 vs the PLT call.

mechanisms.name: Interleaved histogram kernels (4-lane) + lane reduction
mechanisms.details: histogramKeyT<width>/histogramRouteChunkImpl/histogramPidChunkImpl: when lanes != nullptr (engaged for fanout <= HIST_INTERLEAVE_MAX_FANOUT = 2048), counts go to 4 interleaved lane arrays (lanes[k*fanout + p], k = i&3, manually 4x-unrolled main loop) to break the load-increment-store dependency chain; caller-owned, persistent across chunks, reduced once by reduceHistogramLanesImpl (hist[p] += sum of 4 lanes). Counter type is a template (UInt32 and UInt64 exported overloads). countRowsPerShardImpl composes this: allocates 4*num_shards UInt32 lanes only when interleaving applies.

mechanisms.name: Exact uninitialized destination allocation (no memset, first-touch by scatter writes)
mechanisms.details: allocateUninitializedFixed: sample.cloneEmpty() -> reserve(rows) FIRST (fixed-width columns implement reserve via reserve_exact, keeping the allocation exact — this exactness was fixed in commit 100a0114cce) -> insertRawUninitialized(rows) returns the raw span; chassert(raw.size() == rows*sizeOfValueIfFixed). No memset — pages first-touched by the scatter writes themselves (NUMA-friendly). String kernel likewise uses resize_exact on chars and offsets.

mechanisms.name: Variable-length (String) kernel: fused chars + rebased-offsets streams with 32-byte ShardCursor
mechanisms.details: StringScatterState::ShardCursor = {char* chars; UInt64* offsets; UInt64 rebased; UInt64 padding} — exactly 32 bytes so one row touches ONE cache line of cursor state instead of three arrays (header notes at fanout 8192 cursor state alone is 256 KiB). scatterStringChunkImpl per row: copyRowAllowOverflow15 chars copy, chars cursor += len, rebased += len, *offsets++ = rebased (destination offsets are REBASED running per-shard byte totals, never copies of source offsets). Sizing via stringBytesPerShardImpl one-pass byte histogram over (offsets, pids) reading offsets[-1] as 0 through the PODArray left pad. Contract: each shard's chars destination must be its own overflow-tolerant allocation (15-byte overflow forbids carving shards out of one shared buffer). The same ShardCursor is reused by the Array kernel purely as {offsets cursor, rebased element total} storage (chars seeded nullptr).

mechanisms.name: Layer-1 type dispatch: constexpr TypeIndex table, composite kernels, wrapper normalization, exotic fallback
mechanisms.details: KERNEL_ID_TABLE: constexpr array sized 256 (max underlying TypeIndex + 1) filled Fallback; 25 FIXED_WIDTH_TYPES (all int/uint 8..256, BFloat16/Float32/64, UUID, IPv4/6, Decimal32..256, DateTime64, Time64, FixedString) -> FixedWidth; String, Nullable, Tuple, Array, Map, LowCardinality registered; function-pointer table DERIVED from the id table via kernelForId so the trace equals the executed kernel by construction; dispatch is O(1) table[getDataType()]. Composite kernels: Nullable = null map through the width-1 fixed kernel + recursive nested dispatch; Tuple = per-element recursive dispatch with arity guard (element-less tuples: ColumnTuple::create(rows)); Array = per-shard ELEMENT totals + element-level pid expansion + recursive nested dispatch + rebased offsets, with a pre-expansion total_elements > UInt32::max guard that falls back BEFORE materializing the expansion; Map delegates to nested Array(Tuple); LowCardinality single-source = index stream through the fixed kernel + one shared mutated dictionary (multi-source delegates to fallback which merges per-source legacy scatters). ConstCompact: all-const batch with byte-exact equal values (serializeValueIntoArena comparison, never compareAt — preserves +0.0/-0.0 and NaN payloads) -> cloneResized per shard, O(1) memory. Fallback: legacy IColumn::scatter per source + insertRangeFrom merge; also the size_t-safe path when total rows > UInt32::max. Normalization: mayNeedNormalization probes isConst/isSparse/isReplicated OR any subcolumn (deliberately generic, no per-type list); normalizeRepresentation recursively strips Const/Replicated/Sparse at every nesting level, preserving LowCardinality as leaf; hot clean-leaf batches skip it entirely. Introspection: thread_local DispatchTrace (one entry {TypeIndex, ScatterKernelId} per Layer-1 call; disabled cost = one null check per call).

mechanisms.name: AMAC ring driver: 32-slot power-of-two ring, steady/drain split, policy-copy SSA device
mechanisms.details: amac_ring_size = 32 (comment: ~8-10 in-flight rows saturate a core's L1-D miss handling; >32 risks TLB thrashing, cites Kocberber et al. PVLDB 2015; power of two for branch-free wrap); amac_min_rows = 256 degeneration threshold below which the plain sequential loop runs. amacRun<Policy, ring_size=32>(policy, rows): policy contract = Slot type, bool may_grow, start(slot,row)->bool (seed: hash + cursorPlace + home-cell prefetch; false = row handled synchronously, slot stays free — zero-sentinel/skipped rows never enter the ring), step(slot)->AmacStepResult (ONE fused read->act per visit). AmacStepResult: Advance (collision: cursor advanced + next cell prefetched) / Done / DoneNeedsGrow. Steady phase: after priming, while every refill succeeded every slot is provably active, so it sweeps the ring with a plain array for — no per-visit active check, no modulo; first failed refill or row exhaustion drops to the drain loop with the isActive check. run_on_copy opt-in (Policy::copy_into_frame): the driver runs on a frame-local policy copy whose address never escapes so its fields become SSA values that stores through result arrays cannot alias (behind a caller reference they would be reloaded per visit); optional writeBackTo(original) invoked after the drain, skipped on exception.

mechanisms.name: AmacRingSlot layout and state encoding; conditional in-slot hash (no in-ring hashing for cheap keys)
mechanisms.details: AmacRingSlot<false> = {size_t pos; UInt32 row} — static_assert sizeof == 16; AmacRingSlot<true> adds size_t hash — static_assert sizeof == 24. State encoding: no explicit state enum; active/inactive via row == inactive_row sentinel (UInt32::max, hence chassert(rows < inactive_row)); the resume point is just pos (the cell index in the collision chain). cell_stores_hash<Cell> = requires cell.saved_hash: string-key cells (which keep a saved hash as a keyEquals prefilter and would recompute expensively) get the 24-byte slot carrying the hash; cheap-key getters (single/multi-column numeric) RECOMPUTE the hash from the reloaded key per visit, keeping the slot at 16 bytes — measured slot minimalism (a fat slot spills ring state to the stack and kills the MLP the ring exists for). Per-section invariants (map, locators, key getter) live in the policy, not the slot; a policy may extend its slot with address material resolved once at admit (the routed probe carries the leaf's cell buffer and mask).

mechanisms.name: ResumableHashMap cursor API + growth cancellation (amacDrainAndGrow) + compile-time gate
mechanisms.details: ResumableHashMap<Base> DERIVES from the standard join map (cells/hash/grower/public interface unchanged; probe machinery and non-joined iteration see a standard map) and exposes: isZeroKey, cursorPlace(hash)=grower.place, cursorNext(place)=grower.next, cursorCell(place)=&buf[place], cursorCells()=buf (cachable base, invalidated by grow), cursorCellIsEmpty, cursorKeyEquals(cell,key,hash), cursorClaim(cell, key_holder, hash) — exactly emplaceNonZeroImpl up to the mapped-value write (persist key, placement-new cell, setHash, ++m_size), returns grower.overflow(m_size); cursorGrow()=resize(). Correctness invariant: a build policy's step must fuse cell read + mutation into one indivisible visit (batched read-then-mutate would let two in-flight same-key rows both claim one empty cell and silently drop a build row); fused, in-flight rows are equivalent to a sequential insert with rows reordered — safe for an unordered join. amacDrainAndGrow (ALWAYS_INLINE, called from inside the steady loop to avoid capturing policy/ring addresses and forcing per-visit reloads): collects active rows except the just-claimed slot, deactivates them, policy.grow() (the claimed row is fully inserted and gets rehashed by resize), re-seeds collected rows in slot order preserving relative stepping order so same-key rows still act in row order; chassert that every re-seed enters the ring. Gate: amac_join_supported<KeyGetter,Map> = AmacResumableMap<Map> && !LowCardinality getter (its per-dictionary-index dedup cache would fight the ring) && !HashMethodHashed (recomputes a 128-bit serialized-key hash per key-holder fetch); FixedHashMap key8/key16 excluded via the concept (no collision chain, no cursor API).

mechanisms.name: Dense HyperLogLog sketch for leaf hash-table sizing
mechanisms.details: struct DenseHyperLogLog: precision = 13, register_count = 1<<13 = 8192, std::array<UInt8, 8192> registers — 8 KiB flat dense layout, ~1.15% standard error (1.04/sqrt(8192)), covered by the partition plan's reserve safety factor. One sketch per fill lane fed the 32-bit route word of every non-null build key, merged once at the build barrier (merge = element-wise max). add(UInt32 hash): finalize = murmur fmix32 (h^=h>>16; h*=0x85ebca6b; h^=h>>13; h*=0xc2b2ae35; h^=h>>16) — applied because the multiply-shift fold's middle bits are not avalanche-quality for structured keys; the finalizer is a bijection so distinct inputs stay distinct. index = mixed >> (32-13) (top 13 bits); field = low 19 bits; rank = field ? countl_zero(field) - 13 + 1 : 20 (all-zero field maps to max rank 32-precision+1). estimate(): alpha*m^2/sum(2^-rank) with alpha = 0.7213/(1 + 1.079/m), 2^-rank via a function-local static 33-entry ldexp table; linear-counting correction m*ln(m/zeros) when raw <= 2.5m and zeros > 0. Consumed at PartitionedHashJoin.h:214 (per-lane hll), merged in PartitionedHashJoin.cpp:379, fed by computeJoinRoutesForFill (JoinRouteHashing.cpp:142).

mechanisms.name: Fused route-word loops (fill and probe) — confirmation of the port into PartitionedHashJoin
mechanisms.details: In-scope corroboration of the reported fusion: computeJoinRouteWords(key_columns, rows, UInt32* words) is the shared bit-identical word computation (the imported ColumnsScatter route-word family, independent of the leaf tables' CRC32C); computeJoinRoutesForFill(key_columns, rows, const UInt8* skip, UInt16* routes, DenseHyperLogLog& hll) fuses fill consumption into the word loop with NO 32-bit transient — top 16 bits stored per row for ALL rows (scatter reads skipped rows' routes too) and the full word feeds the sketch only where skip does not filter; computeJoinLeafIds(key_columns, rows, bits, UInt16* leaf_ids) fuses the probe-side leaf-id derivation word >> (32-bits) directly (agrees with the build's stored-route slice route >> (16-bits) for all 0 < bits <= 16). Additionally, the fusion hook inside ColumnsScatter itself: scatterKeyChunk emits pids as a by-product of the route computation when pids_out != nullptr (RouteFromKey::partition), so payload columns can reload pids instead of rehashing.
